audit.whatIsWrong: Aegis Assault is described as a blanket damage negation — "blocks your Q Stretching Strikes damage entirely", "negates your Q auto-damage during his combo".
audit.why: Riot's text is "Pantheon sets his shield, becoming invulnerable to damage from the front". It is directional, not absolute. Told it blocks everything, a Zac player walks away from a trade he could have won by attacking from the other side; told it blocks the front, the same player has an actual instruction. Aegis Assault is also 22/21/20/19/18s — the longest non-ultimate cooldown in Pantheon's kit and never once quantified in the entry.
audit.corrected: Aegis Assault blocks damage from the front only, on 22s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shield Vault is called a stun throughout but its auto-attack reset is never mentioned.
audit.why: Shield Vault carries an auto-attack reset, so the burst that follows the stun arrives a full attack sooner than the animation suggests. Together with Mortal Will empowering every few casts, that is why the level 2-5 all-in front-loads harder than its ability damage alone implies.
audit.corrected: Shield Vault is a 13s dash-stun that also resets his auto.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grand Starfall is described as giving "roam and dive pressure" with no range and no cooldown.
audit.why: It is 5500 range on 180/165/150s. Both numbers matter and neither was stated: 5500 tells the Zac player that a Pantheon who vanishes is landing in another lane rather than recalling, and 180s at rank 1 tells them how long the map is safe afterwards.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Pantheon 6 of 7 stages against a 54.69% Zac record over 128 games.
audit.why: Pantheon genuinely owns levels 1 through 6, so most of the chart is right and I did not invent Zac windows to pad it. The first-item stage is the one that does not hold: that is where Zac's health item starts absorbing a burst pattern that has stopped growing, and the full layer's own phases[] already reads Zac there. Moving that single stage to Skill is the honest correction; the rest of the win rate is earned after laning, which the last stage already reflects.
audit.corrected: Pantheon levels 1-6, Skill at first item, Zac at 2+ items.

audit.why: The advice to farm through the early deficit rather than contest it is right and is supported by the kits — Comet Spear out-ranges Zac's approach and Shield Vault punishes the slingshot commit.

notes: Packet suspectName 'Let's Bounce' is a FALSE POSITIVE — disk already reads "Let's Bounce!"; the detector strips the exclamation mark. No wrong ability names in this matchup. DO NOT APPLY the _missing-interactions.json headline for this pairing: it claims "Your Elastic Slingshot (E) shuts off Pantheon's Shield Vault (W), Grand Starfall (R)", which is derived from a grounding flag on Zac's E. That flag is a false positive from the phrase 'attaches his arms to the ground' in Riot's description — Elastic Slingshot grounds nobody. The same bogus flag is generating dash-denial headlines for Zac across the whole library and should be stripped at the derive step (tools/derive-interactions.js). UNVERIFIED, left alone: the existing claim that Shield Vault interrupts Zac's R animation. A stun plausibly does, but Zac's kit file carries no channel or interruptible flag on R and needsResearch is empty, so I left the sentence intact rather than reinforcing it. SYSTEMIC: content win[] (Pantheon x6, Zac) and full phases[].side (Pantheon, Skill, Zac, Zac, Pantheon, Zac, Zac) disagree badly — I moved content win[5] to Skill, which narrows the gap without inventing a Zac window, but the two layers still disagree at indices 1, 2 and 3. phases[].side cannot be repaired through apply-proposals.js, which rejects full-layer edits whose `before` is under 12 characters.
